clue.text: Sanctimonious bounder or beastly fighting man

parts.note: pi is informal British for smugly pious, sanctimonious
a cad is a dishonourable man, a bounder

explanation.surface: A self-righteous rotter, or perhaps a brutal combatant, is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' is not an insult here: the fighting man fights beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A mounted bullfighter who lances the bull is a combatant in a contest with an animal.

clue.text: The average well-practised story

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
able means skilled, competent

explanation.surface: A tale told with ordinary competence.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple tale illustrating a moral lesson is a kind of story.

clue.text: Not in favour of more substantial scientific apparatus

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
denser means thicker, more solid

explanation.surface: Someone opposes a heavier piece of lab equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that cools vapour into liquid, or stores charge, is laboratory equipment.

clue.text: See fit soldier retreating — in retreat

indicators.note: the reversed soldier sits inside the word for retreat

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

indicators.note: the soldier goes backwards, its letters read in reverse

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier falling back into a hiding place thinks it wise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns GI into IG, which goes into DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To condescend to do something is to think it worthy of oneself, to choose to do it.

clue.text: The queen of Canadian cities

explanation.surface: One place is hailed as the finest of Canada's towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for queen, used in royal titles; also the capital city of Saskatchewan.

clue.text: Giving to a couple of hundred a word of thanks for the music

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two of them give CC
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone tips a couple of hundred with a thank-you in return for a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard showpiece of rapid passages is a kind of musical composition.

clue.text: A refreshing feature of the educational system

definitions.text: A refreshing feature of the educational system

parts.words: A refreshing feature of the educational system
parts.note: read literally, a place in a school where pupils buy snacks and refreshments

explanation.surface: Something reviving within the way schools are organised.
explanation.definitionFit: A school kiosk selling sweets and snacks is where pupils get refreshment.

clue.text: Trouble must be taken about handle for an ornamental panel

indicators.note: the word for trouble goes around the word for handle

parts.note: care means trouble or worry, as in taking care
to touch is to handle

explanation.surface: Care is needed when handling a decorative plaque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' and 'handle' look like a warning about handling; 'must be taken about' is the container signal, the first piece wrapping the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An oval scroll-shaped frame, as round Egyptian royal names, is a decorative tablet.

clue.text: Bringing a highly-qualified person in with all speed

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, holds a higher degree

explanation.surface: Bringing in a graduate as quickly as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word meaning at full force or with great haste.

clue.text: A surprisingly chaste and loyal friend

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters end up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A loyal companion is unexpectedly pure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' is the anagram signal on 'chaste'. Achates is the faithful companion of Aeneas in Virgil's Aeneid, so his name stands for a loyal friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of Aeneas's faithful comrade became a byword for a devoted companion.

clue.text: Call to restrain a worker delivering a tirade

indicators.note: the word for call holds the worker inside it, as if restraining it

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: Telephoning to rein in an employee who is shouting angrily.
explanation.definitionFit: Raving loudly and at length is the behaviour of someone giving an angry harangue.

clue.text: Involved in a crash, possibly a quarter come out of it without a mark

definitions.text: come out of it without a mark

indicators.note: the letter for the compass quarter is wrapped up within the other letters
signals that the letters of a crash may be rearranged

parts.note: W, west, is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: After a car accident, one corner of the vehicle somehow escapes undamaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges A CRASH to CARASH, and W goes inside it. The definition is cryptic: cars come out of this place spotless.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehicles pass through a car-cleaning facility and emerge spotless, free of dirt marks.

clue.text: Preoccupation with a buzzing in the ears?

explanation.surface: An obsession described as a buzzing heard close to the head.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an obsessive fixation; literally, an insect buzzing inside one's hat near the ears.

clue.text: A woman in extremity — turned out

indicators.note: the woman's name is placed inside the word for extremity

parts.note: an end is an extremity, the furthest point
Sue is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman in dire straits was thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow as a result is to happen afterwards, as things that came to pass did.

clue.text: Regard beaming as a bloomer

parts.note: to eye is to regard, look at
bright means beaming, shining

explanation.surface: Someone views a radiant smile as a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake; it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wild flower once used for eye ailments is a flowering plant.

clue.text: Combines caught over apparently sure things

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
on can mean over, as in a lid on a pot
certs is informal British for certainties, sure bets

explanation.surface: Agricultural harvesters seized on what look like safe bets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combines' suggests farm harvesters; it is a verb meaning acts in unison. 'apparently' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in concert is to join forces, to coordinate or unite efforts.

clue.text: Service holiday-accommodation — one takes on the maintenance

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army service
a tent is accommodation for a camping holiday
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A holiday service where someone undertakes the upkeep.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping or holding on to something is preserving it, maintaining it.

clue.text: May well be silent when presented to Her Majesty in Eire

indicators.note: the anagram is put in front of the royal letters
suggests the letters of silent could equally form another word

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone may keep quiet when introduced to the Queen in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May well be' is the anagram signal on 'silent', and 'when presented to' places it before the royal letters. The definition is just 'in Eire', naming a province of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four provinces of Ireland, containing Dublin, is a region of that country.

clue.text: A down-to earth individual producing colourful results

definitions.text: A down-to earth individual producing colourful results

parts.words: A down-to earth individual producing colourful results
parts.note: read literally, a person who works down in the soil and grows bright flowers

explanation.surface: A practical, unpretentious person whose work turns out vivid.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tending flower beds works in the soil and grows bright blooms.

clue.text: Joke about reel, though out of breath

indicators.note: the word for joke goes around the word for reel

parts.note: a gag is a joke
to reel is to spin round

explanation.surface: A comedian jokes about dancing a reel despite being winded.
explanation.definitionFit: Panting, struggling for air, describes someone breathless.

clue.text: The warmer man a better-half will follow

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: only the second half of the word better is used, the first half dropped

explanation.surface: A husband warms to his wife, who follows behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better-half' looks like the wife; here it is half of the word BETTER, its last three letters TER, and 'will follow' puts the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiator or stove is an appliance that warms a room.

clue.text: Arrange the letters again and note the time

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a spell is a period of time

explanation.surface: Instructions to rearrange the letters and note the time.
explanation.definitionFit: To write out a word with different letters is to give it a new spelling.

clue.text: Secure the proceeds of salvage

indicators.note: what results from working over the letters of secure

explanation.surface: Getting hold of the money raised from a salvage operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the proceeds of' is the anagram signal: SECURE, worked over, yields its letters reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving something from loss or wreck is to rescue it.

clue.text: Set tinned prunes out for the directors

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Lay out tinned prunes for the board members.
explanation.definitionFit: Supervisors in charge of an organisation or department are its managers or heads.

clue.text: Stick by egghead

parts.note: past means by, as in walking past or by
the head, or first letter, of egg

explanation.surface: Stay close to an intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' suggests an intellectual; it is the first letter of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue made from flour and water is an adhesive used to fix things together.

clue.text: A poet in politics — a pedant elected into parliament

indicators.note: the poet is found sitting inside the words, like a member inside a chamber

explanation.surface: A versifying pedant is voted into parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet is hidden in 'pedant elected'. Dante served in Florentine government before exile.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine author of the Divine Comedy was also a city magistrate.

clue.text: May be seen as a perceptive faculty

explanation.surface: Something visible is described as a power of perception.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, IN SIGHT means visible.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrase, visible; as one word, the faculty of deep understanding or discernment.

clue.text: Bound to look at choice

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or examine
fine means choice, excellent

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to examine a selection.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict or limit within bounds is to keep something enclosed.

clue.text: Greek consumer getting to be of more importance

parts.note: an eater is one who consumes

explanation.surface: A Greek diner is becoming more significant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigger in significance or rank is the comparative of large or important.

clue.text: Going on and on, so are lent change

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of these letters

explanation.surface: Lent seems endless, so let it be altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting forever without end describes something that never stops.
